top_choice_rationale: P003 pairs two achievements that each meet the game-changer test with a clean attribution. Base editing rests on a simple chemical idea, deamination of a nucleobase by an engineered deaminase guided by a Cas nickase, which gave programmable single-base conversion without a double-strand break. It has been independently reproduced and is in first-in-human studies, and naming Liu alone keeps the citation about a chemical principle. Car-Parrinello is a two-author 1985 paper with four decades of independent validation and a quantitative link to experiment. I rank lipid nanoparticles next for its physical-chemical design principle, and C-N coupling third because the 2010 prize already honoured Pd cross-coupling. Sequencing sits below them because it is a crowded-credit platform, and no award is last.
recusal_note: No direct conflict apparent from profile. Car-Parrinello is in my own field of computational chemistry and I know Warshel's EVB school, but I have no stated personal tie to Car, Parrinello or Liu.
